Bir Sreshtho Matiur Rahman: Memorial bears scars of neglect
2026-08-22T01:16:18+06:00 | Our Correspondent, Narsingdi
https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/bir-sreshtho-matiur-rahman-memorial-bears-scars-neglect-4253631

The 55th death anniversary of Bir Sreshtho Flight Lieutenant Matiur Rahman, who embraced martyrdom while fighting for Bangladesh’s independence in 1971, was observed in Narsingdi on Thursday.

To commemorate his memory, a memorial was built at Mahmudabad along the Dhaka-Sylhet highway, while a library and a museum were established in his village in 2008. However, the museum has yet to take complete shape, and his ancestral home has remained neglected for years.

Matiur Rahman was martyred on August 20, 1971, during the Liberation War. His childhood was closely tied to Ramnagar village in Raipura upazila, later renamed Bir Sreshtho Matiur Nagar in recognition of his supreme sacrifice. To mark the day, the Raipura upazila administration, along with political, social and cultural organisations, organised daylong programmes.

Locals expressed frustration over the lack of initiatives to preserve Matiur’s memory. A recent visit found damaged walls and seating areas near the entrance of Ramnagar High School, while the library, though housing around 4,200 books, has not received new additions since 2008.

The memorial museum remains in poor condition, with no permanent display of Matiur Rahman’s personal belongings, documents or memorabilia. Visitors often leave disappointed.

Locals alleged that drug abusers gather on the premises at night, tarnishing the site’s dignity.

Imran Hossain, a local youth, said, “The sacrifice of Bir Sreshtho Matiur Rahman is a matter of pride for us. But it is disappointing that there is no memorabilia of him in the museum.”

Mamun Mia, a former member of Mosapur Union Parishad, said the area should have received more facilities as the birthplace of a national hero.

Librarian Beauty Akter said donated personal belongings remain packed in boxes due to lack of display arrangements. She added that waterlogging during the rainy season and broken electric lights further damage the facility.

Raipura Upazila Nirbahi Officer Md Masud said the museum and library are operated under the supervision of the district council, and the administration will take necessary measures to address the issues.
